Even during those low times, my thoughts are still racing and piling on top of each other.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how long these periods of feeling 'way up' and then very low typically last, and do you notice any patterns or triggers that seem to set them off?\n\nPatient: These high-energy phases have been going on almost constantly for the past year and a half, only easing up briefly before flaring again and leaving me feeling completely flat. It all really started when I began pushing myself so hard to become a CNA supervisor, taking on extra shifts and night classes that totally disrupted my routine.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if these high-energy phases and low periods occur in distinct episodes that last for days or weeks at a time, or if they can shift back and forth within the same day?\n\nPatient: No, they aren't quick changes within the same day. These are long stretches lasting for weeks at a time where I feel completely revved up and barely sleep for days, only easing up for a little bit before starting right back up.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many of these distinct high-energy and low periods you've experienced over the past year and a half, and do you recall any specific events or circumstances that seemed to trigger the switch from one phase to the other?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how many distinct times it's happened because it feels like it's been going on almost constantly since I started pushing for the promotion. It has really impacted my ability to keep up with my charting at work and has caused me to fall behind in my classes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, over the past year and a half where you felt completely normal, without either the high-energy or low phases, and if so, how long those periods lasted?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I haven't really felt completely normal at all since this started a year and a half ago, as I've spent almost the whole time either highly revved up or coming down but still feeling keyed up. It has really impacted my ability to keep up with my charting at work and has caused me to fall behind in my classes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, over the past year and a half where you felt completely normal, without either the high-energy or low phases, and if so, how long those periods lasted?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I haven't really felt completely normal at all since this started a year and a half ago, as I've spent almost the whole time either highly revved up or coming down but still feeling keyed up. There was a brief spell last winter where my mood and energy dropped back to a \"so-so\" level, but even then I didn't feel normal because I was still hearing whispers and felt convinced people were trying to sabotage me.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of depression, with each episode lasting for at least two weeks, over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: I don't think I've had distinct, two-week-long depressive episodes like that. While I do have times where I feel flat, inactive, and lose interest in my hobbies, my main struggles have really been the high-energy phases and the racing thoughts or suspiciousness. It has never really felt like a clear episode of deep depression.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if, during those times when you felt flat and inactive, you experienced significant depressive symptoms such as feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or recurrent thoughts of death, which lasted for at least two weeks?\n\nPatient: I don't recall having those specific feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or thoughts of death. Instead, my low periods have felt more like being completely flat, drained of life, and just lacking any energy to do the things I used to enjoy.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any periods where you felt extremely happy or irritable for at least four consecutive days, and if so, did you notice any changes in your sleep patterns, energy levels, or engagement in activities during those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, I experience those stretches frequently, feeling either way up and overexcited or extremely touchy and irritable over small things. During these times, my sleep drops to just three or four hours a night but I still wake up feeling completely wired. My energy levels skyrocket, and I find myself buzzing around cleaning, starting multiple art projects, and taking on extra shifts because I just can't sit still.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether your high-energy phases and low periods have been interspersed with periods of relatively normal mood, or have they predominantly been one after the other without a return to a baseline mood in between?\n\nPatient: I really haven't returned to my normal baseline mood for most of this time. I've spent the vast majority of the past year and a half either highly revved up or just coming down from those highs while still feeling more keyed up than my old self. The only real exception was a period during the winter where my energy and mood dropped back to a \"so-so\" level, but even then I didn't feel quite back to normal.\n\nDoctor: Can you specify if these episodes of high energy and low mood have occurred in a pattern that resembles a regular cycle, or have they been more sporadic and unpredictable over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: It doesn't really feel like a neat, predictable cycle at all. Most of the time, I've just been either completely revved up or coming down from it.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if the periods of high energy and the periods of feeling low have been occurring in a way that you can clearly distinguish one episode from another, or do they tend to blend together over time?\n\nPatient: They definitely tend to blend together rather than being clearly separate.
